Perfect Game #37, Hacknet.  This game is very clever and it will make you feel stupid and dumb at the same time.  Hacknet fits a very small niche, but it fits it perfectly.  Using mostly realistic commands and functions it really feels like you're hacking these machines, and it's a lot of fun.  The different machines you enter are all unique and have a lot of fun text files or logs of chatrooms.  The story is interesting as well, and your actions do have an impact.  It can be intense when you have a time limit to complete a task, but it can also feel frustrating when you're stuck and not really sure what to do.  It's a great experience, but I wouldn't recommend it to most people just because of how niche it is.

hacknet is a video game that allows you to perform simulated computer hacking. it released in august of 2015 and was developed by australian indie dev matt trobbiani and published by fellow traveler, a australian video game publisher. who were founded in 2011. this is the second game they have published on steam, and having played three of their published games before (vertiginous golf (2014), orwell: ignorance is strength (2018) and neo cab (2019)), with hacknet (2015) being the fourth game of theirs I have played (as well as the first orwell game that was self-published by the developer). fellow traveler has a unique eye for interesting narrative games, but early in their company's history, they placed a focus on australian devs, including hacknet's solo developer.

hacknet simulates hacking, and does it exceptionally well. it doesn't overwhelm players at any point, but is complex enough to make you feel like you're actually doing something interesting, even though you're clearly playing a game. you'll do things like infiltrate a computer remotely, and once you're inside, find files and other things you could delete, including something like deleting system files to destroy the computer essentially. all the while you're unfolding this intriguing narrative as you investigate someone's death and whether it was really an accident as reported by the media. it actually opens up after a brief tutorial and allows really open-ended gameplay throughout the rest of the game all the way until the main plot finishes. 

there's also a really awesome DLC titled 'labyrinths' that is essentially a whole sequel to the base game, but it's only sold as DLC. it's definitely worth it and i recommend that as it's also a major improvement upon the base game, which is already extremely good as far as hacking sims go. it was supposed to come out in december 2016 but was delayed and eventually released on march 31st, 2017. it implements a bunch of new hacking tools/features, and about 3-4 hours of gameplay on top of the base game.

you can routinely find this on sale for like a dollar and a half, which is a insane value for the base game, with the DLC being a little more expensive even when on sale, but again, it's a major improvement and worth the extra three dollars or so. this is definitely the best hacking sim game i have ever seen, and definitely worth grabbing on sale at such cheap prices.

I'll make this review spoiler free as the game is much more enjoyable when everything is a surprise. The game is insanely fun, truly like nothing I've ever played before. It's like the Superhot of hacking games. Throughout the game you'll uncover many different programs to assist you on your mission. The game features an active story-line but throws everything at the player at once. In my play through I found it helpful and almost required to use tutorials. Some areas of the game are far too confusing for new players to understand.[spoiler] like when Naix hacks you [/spoiler]

If you use guides I recommend using them sparingly as although receiving light spoilers the game still surprise me in many ways. I bought the game on sale and I recommend you do so too. Although being such an amazing game albiet a bit confusing, a $10 price tag feels like a bit much for this game. I strongly recommend buying the DLC as well as it ties nicely into the game, but do be warned about it's appearance early into the game. 

I'll keep this part about the DLC short and sweet and spoilers will be hidden in well, spoilers. The mission for the DLC appears very early on and although saying its a complex mission, the game doesn't nearly give you enough briefing for what you are getting into. I would STRONGLY suggest starting the DLC after you do at least half of the /spoiler CSEC missions which are available later game. 

Overall, I found the game very enjoyable and the use of the game's idea and to what extent it was carried out to was AMAZING! Although I would reference an area in the DLC I found it slightly glitchy but if it works for you, is quiet enjoyable. 

I would personally recommend this game to anybody who has time on their hands and is looking for a game that can get you energized quick! This game has permanently secured a home as one of my favorite and most enjoyable gaming experiences and I would strongly recommend giving it a try!

Hacknet  Это игра, где ты убиваешь порты, или ты сам есть порты, где ты убиваешь самыми изощренными способами порты. То есть там можно придумать свою определённую местность, то есть можешь придумать ту же школу с портами, также взорвать её порты, убить учетки, но там более изощрённая ситуация. То есть там не изготавливаешь forkbomb, тебе даётся различное хацкерское по, ты можешь обмениватся. Почему называется «hack-net» — там идёт трейд различными софтинками, уничтожения порты. Там вытаскивают, например, специальное оружие, чтобы вытаскивать сообщения в течение 90 секунд. То есть это вот длится 90 секунд.

Hacknet is a hacking simulator that you play from a simulated command line and the story is told entirely through text. Your friend has been killed and they sent you the powerful new hacking tool they've been working on - it allows you to automatically access any computer you know the address for. Using this tool you'll investigate their death and uncover a conspiracy.

I really enjoyed this one, the majority of gameplay has you running commands and exploring computers, downloading files, and running scripts to investigate the crazy story going on in the background. There are a few twists and turns, some surprise gameplay sections, and it all builds up to a dramatic finale.

I will say that gameplay can get repetitive since you're running the same few commands over and over and the game itself is not very long, but personally I found it enjoyable. If you're looking for that hacker feeling the game lets you live the fantasy of hopping from computer to computer stealing data, deleting logs, and coming up against different kinds of challenges. The layout is very charming and the story is fun even if it's not very surprising.

Points for originality and a simple game design executed well.
